chunks: 4559 - Harun ibn Muslim narrated from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad, who said:

Ten categories of bondwomen are prohibited: you may not combine between a mother and her daughter; nor between two sisters; nor your bondwoman when she is pregnant by someone other than you until she delivers; nor your bondwoman when she is your paternal aunt through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is your maternal aunt through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is your sister through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she is the daughter of your brother through breastfeeding; nor your bondwoman when she has a husband; nor your bondwoman when she is in a waiting period ('iddah); nor your bondwoman when another shares ownership in her with you.

key_terms.الْأُخْتَيْنِ: two sisters, whom one may not combine together
key_terms.حَامِلٌ: pregnant, here meaning pregnant by another man
key_terms.زَوْجٌ: a husband, indicating she is already married
key_terms.شَرِيكٌ: a co-owner who shares ownership in the bondwoman
key_terms.عِدَّةٍ: the waiting period after separation or widowhood

ai.seo_question: Which categories of bondwomen are prohibited in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out ten legal prohibitions concerning relations with bondwomen. It addresses unlawful combinations based on kinship, fosterage, pregnancy, marriage, waiting period, and shared ownership, reflecting detailed fiqh rulings on lawful and unlawful sexual relations.
